info.title: Decionis Commerce Gate API
info.description: Canonical Commerce Gate contract for the synchronous ERP guard and the tenant-bound Decionis Protocol operations used by the local Commerce Gate MCP adapter, plus the licensed AWS historical assessment and synthetic trial features on the Commerce API.

post.summary: Validate one bounded ERP transaction through Commerce Gate
post.description: Deprecated alias of `POST /v1/connections/{connectionId}/executions`: the same handler, which answers this sales contract unchanged for the installed Business Central extension 1.0.2.3 and MCP clients. Performs enforced binary policy validation and atomic agent-budget authorization for a complete Dynamics 365 transaction. It returns ALLOW or BLOCK but never writes, posts, releases, or modifies the ERP transaction. After policy clears, the candidate backend rejects a changed request for a tracked transaction when its timestamp is equal to or older than the stored revision, returning HTTP 200/BLOCK with AGENT_BUDGET_REQUEST_CONFLICT without changing the reservation or spent amount. Exact current retries reuse their budget result; strictly newer revisions undergo budget authorization. Transaction identity normalizes only tenant UUID casing, preserving organization, agent and transaction identifiers. One equivalent legacy reservation retains its original stored key. Multiple equivalent reservations return the same conflict and leave all rows and spent amount unchanged for reconciliation. This requires a configured agent budget and the matching backend deployment; it is not a wall-clock expiry rule or the sixteen-check Protocol preflight.

200.description: Central binary decision, including budget revision conflicts as BLOCK

get.summary: Resolve the registered company context for payment evidence
get.description: Uses the current ordinary workspace key to resolve Core's synchronized Accounts workspace, exact active verified Business Central company connection and current revision-bound native read grant. The key must have decision:read and decision:write; it is independent of Decionis-managed provider credentials. Returns non-secret registration metadata only: basis=persisted_connection_and_native_grant, provider_read_authority=not_checked, execution_available=false unless Decionis issues single-use permits for this connection, when it is true; a permit, never the flag, lets a payment post. The native shell must compare the returned tenant, environment and company with its actual session before saving this context. Payment and settlement calls compare every pinned assertion with fresh Core metadata again. No body or query parameters are accepted. This source candidate does not read Microsoft payment facts, refresh provider authority, or grant financial posting permission, and requires the matching Core and Commerce deployments.

200.description: Current registered company metadata; no provider read or execution authority

post.summary: Observe or enforce one ERP vendor payment against the tenant's payment checks
post.description: Deprecated alias of `POST /v1/connections/{connectionId}/executions`: the same handler, which answers this payment contract unchanged for the installed Business Central extension 1.0.2.3. The Payment Release Guard. A native ERP shell states one vendor payment it is releasing and the facts it holds; Commerce Gate asks Decionis to evaluate it as a commerce-preflight-v2 PAYMENT_RELEASE with the caller's own organization key and answers the tenant's policy for P12 payment release authority, P13 duplicate invoice, P14 beneficiary change window and P15 liquidity floor. In OBSERVE mode the shell asks after posting, Decionis records a Shadow decision and `enforced` is false: nothing is blocked. In ENFORCE mode the shell asks before posting, Decionis records an enforced decision, `enforced` is true, and the shell stops the posting on HOLD or BLOCK; an enforced request states no posted entry (400 PAYMENT_ENFORCE_AFTER_POSTING). Commerce Gate only answers: nothing here initiates, holds, routes or settles a payment. Account numbers never cross this boundary; the beneficiary facts carry only when the vendor's bank account last changed and whether that change was verified. Business Central requires the full native_context captured from the context endpoint. Core rechecks the current workspace key, connection and native read grant; every organization, workspace environment, tenant, company, environment name and revision assertion must match. Registration metadata does not independently verify the native shell's payment facts or authorize posting. The resolved metadata and its evidence boundary remain in the saved evidence and response. Exact OBSERVE retries return the saved receipt; ENFORCE retries recheck the original upstream decision without replacing it. A separate after-post OBSERVE result does not change an earlier ENFORCE decision. F&SCM retains its existing credential/tenant binding and does not accept native_context. A 502 means Decionis did not return a bound evaluation in the requested mode, and a 503 PAYMENT_ENFORCEMENT_DISABLED means enforcement is switched off centrally; an observing shell retries and an enforcing shell applies its own fallback mode. This is an unreleased source candidate that needs the matching backend and a tenant policy whose allowed sources include the ERP's source name.

200.description: The tenant's policy answer; enforced exactly when the request was ENFORCE

post.summary: Report bank settlement of observed ERP payments
post.description: After posting, the native ERP shell reports whether each observed payment has been matched to a bank statement. Commerce Gate records drift when a payment stays unsettled past the company's window (payment_unsettled, cleared once it settles or is voided) or settles at a different amount than it posted (payment_settled_mismatch, which a person reviews). Business Central uses the same current workspace key and full native_context checks as payment validation. Each item must match a saved posted OBSERVE anchor, including its exact entry_id, payment, vendor, amount and currency. event_id and sequence are immutable per-payment event identity; exact retries do not count twice, stale sequences do not change drift, and settled or voided payments cannot reopen. Reusing an event identity with different facts returns 409; a batch commits atomically. The envelope timestamp is excluded from event identity and is not an independently verified occurrence time. F&SCM retains its existing credential/tenant behavior. Nothing is sent to Decionis, no account data crosses the boundary, and nothing moves money. A 503 means the report was not recorded and the ERP should retry. This is an unreleased source candidate.

post.summary: Create an execution and hold its single-use permit (permit wire profile)
post.description: agent-safe.executors.native/1 §5, step 1. A native platform states one action in its own words (a Business Central payment line or sales document); the executor host resolves the connection from the caller's key, prepares the action, asks Decionis to decide it and bind a single-use grant to its exact intent, and holds the grant unclaimed. HELD returns the permit (permit_id, intent_sha256, expires_at); every other decision returns BLOCKED with its reason codes and no permit. A payment permit is bound to one payment line: company, journal template and batch, line number, the line's own id, vendor, beneficiary-account hash, amount and currency. Posting the legacy payment or sales body here is answered exactly as at its deprecated alias.

200.description: HELD with the permit, or BLOCKED with why

get.summary: Read one execution at the executor host
get.description: Where one execution is: HELD, CLAIMED, SETTLED or BLOCKED, its outcome, decision, permit and the finalization the authority recorded. Only the connection that created it can read it, at its current revision.

post.summary: Present the permit once, immediately before posting
post.description: The platform presents the permit_id it was issued; the executor host claims the grant with Decionis, once. A permit already presented, expired, or for another execution is refused, and a second presentation never reaches the authority.

post.summary: Report the native posting receipt, which settles the execution
post.description: The platform's posting capture reports what it posted (or that the posting rolled back) in its own vocabulary. The executor reads the receipt against the permit's exact line; Decionis records the outcome on the grant. A receipt is accepted once; a second one, or one for a permit nobody presented, is refused and changes nothing.

200.description: SETTLED with the outcome, or REFUSED with why

post.summary: Reconcile an execution whose posting nobody can state
post.description: For an execution whose receipt never came or could not be read. The executor is asked, read-only, what the platform later stated about the line; a proven answer is recorded with Decionis, and an unknown one stays unknown. Nothing is ever posted again.

post.summary: Record one tenant-bound commerce action evaluation in Shadow Mode
post.description: The Commerce Gate MCP always submits SHADOW and requires the response to confirm SHADOW. `commercegate_evaluate_action` accepts all eleven canonical commerce action types: the seven published families and the four finance families (payment release, vendor bank change, early-payment discount and credit-hold release) of the unreleased commerce-preflight-v2 source candidate, which require a matching backend and never move money. For the live Walmart Marketplace connector, Commerce Evaluation, Price Guard, Order Guard, order interception, margin protection, release, hold, and cancel map to those canonical preflights. Order acceptance and price change use native margin mappings; inventory, fulfillment, promotion, refund, and return are generic Protocol evaluations whose outcome depends on the tenant policy and supplied signals. The unreleased commerce-preflight-v2 opt-in adds sixteen explicit policy checks with a matching backend and a server-owned policy bundle. It binds the result to the action, facts, policy version and idempotency key; missing required facts or unsupported checks hold the proposal. The candidate Commerce /aws facade preserves the original action/result key through its separately authenticated commerce-preflight-transport-v1 retry namespace. Its context.commerce_preflight_transport marker is reserved service metadata, not a tool argument. This does not establish hosted availability. It does not add native execution paths. `commercegate_evaluate_marketplace_offer_submission` accepts a separate, bounded Microsoft Partner Center or AWS Marketplace SaaS offer packet with digest-bound release evidence. Either evaluation can create decision evidence but never executes a marketplace action or submits an offer.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Stable key reused for retries of the same proposed action.

200.description: Shadow Mode evaluation and evidence references

post.summary: Evaluate a labelled synthetic sample in a verified AgentSaaS trial
post.description: Requires a source-verified active trial. The server generates a synthetic SHADOW proposal; callers cannot supply customer data, policy, organization, execution mode or transaction payloads. The actual Protocol decision is returned without promising a particular outcome. At most 10,000 unique evaluations are admitted across the 14-day trial. Replays reuse the same idempotency key and never consume an additional slot. Expiry and the cap stop new evaluations without paid overage or automatic paid conversion. This additive trial feature does not replace the paid governance APIs. Billing/trial activation is default-off until deployment validation.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional; must match idempotency_key in the JSON body.

200.description: Actual synthetic Shadow evaluation; not cacheable

402.description: Trial evaluation allowance exhausted; no charge is created

get.summary: List licensed synthetic and connected-store historical assessment sources
get.description: Requires deployed, enabled AWS historical routes and a current AWS/Account license. The organization comes only from the credential. Lists the versioned synthetic example and supported stores already connected to that organization; no new registration, store connection or trial entitlement is created. AgentOps managed HTTP helpers use this API; the local STDIO MCP inventory is unchanged. Commerce Gate uses the purchase-session BFF separately.

200.description: Bounded source choices; no credentials or customer payloads

post.summary: Assess a bounded previous-90-day history without executing commerce actions
post.description: Additive historical feature; it does not replace the existing governance APIs. Requires deployed, enabled AWS historical routes and a current licensed credential. The server fixes the previous 90-day window by transaction time. Accepts only a supported connected-store UUID or the labelled synthetic dataset, never raw transactions, organization, dates or a policy override. Reusing a request key returns the immutable original result; rebinding its source returns 409. Responses are at most 100 KiB, with at most 100 records assessed. Partial history, missing item costs and timestamp gaps remain visible. Results measure merchandise margin only, excluding shipping, taxes and payment or platform fees. Inline results are unsigned, with null proof_ref; no signed dossier is claimed. Synthetic examples use an explicit sample 12 percent floor, never a guessed customer policy. A verified 14-day AWS trial uses its actual entitlement expiry; this endpoint never starts or extends a trial. No platform or AWS usage write.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: If supplied, must equal the required body idempotency_key.

requestBody.description: Maximum 2 KiB; no extra fields accepted.

200.description: Immutable completed or failed assessment; failures contain stable error codes

get.summary: Read one immutable assessment bound to the current organization and AWS grant
get.description: Requires deployed, enabled AWS historical routes. Every read rechecks the current license, credential revocation and expiry. No organization query argument is accepted. Results contain minimized unsigned historical evidence, not live transaction payloads or execution authority. At most 100 KiB.

200.description: Exact stored assessment, including its original source and 90-day window

post.description: Binds the run to the credential's organization. The objective fixes the admissible action families; the platform scope, action budget, currency-exposure budget and horizon (at most 31 days) bound every later proposal. The same idempotency key replays the same run; a rebound key is 409. writes: true lets the run carry writes, each still decided by Core with the agent as actor. Nothing is evaluated or executed.

post.summary: Record an evaluated proposal under the run
post.description: A PROCEED must cite a dossier; every cited dossier is read from Core with the caller's credential and must belong to the organization and, where it carries a decision, agree with the recorded outcome. Each recorded proposal consumes one action; a PROCEED with an amount consumes exposure in the budget currency. Out-of-objective, out-of-scope, wrong-currency, expired or over-budget proposals are refused with a reason code, consume nothing, and close the run where a budget is exhausted. Without write, recording never executes the proposal. In a run with writes, a write (a Walmart price change, order acknowledgement or cancellation, a Business Central payment line or sales document release) is made only from the run's own AGENT key (otherwise 403) and is captured as an intent with the agent as actor: Core decides it like a person's write, ALLOW runs the platform's executor once, a hold opens a decision case with the agent's draft, and Business Central decides its writes when it posts the line or releases the document. The receipt's write states the outcome; a write is never retried.

post.description:
Every request authenticates through the Decionis authority, which checks
Accounts-issued OAuth access against current source authority. Caller
organization headers cannot establish authority. Query credentials and
browser Origin headers are rejected. Supply exactly one Authorization or
x-api-key header. Requests
have a 100 KiB body limit and finite processing, authority and rate-store
bounds. This transport does not support batch messages, GET event streams
or resumable sessions. Notifications return 202 without a response body.

WWW-Authenticate.description:
Included only when OAuth is enabled. A Bearer challenge identifies
the configured resource_metadata URL and fixed Commerce scopes.

403.description: Origin, organization, role, scope, tool or OAuth resource denied

429.description: Rate limit exceeded; Retry-After and X-RateLimit headers included

503.description: Authority, durable limiter or storage unavailable, or capacity exhausted

get.summary: Discover the configured Commerce MCP OAuth resource
get.description:
Registered only when COMMERCE_MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED=1 and both canonical
HTTPS resource and issuer URLs are configured. Otherwise this route is
absent. The document is static public metadata; no authority, identity,
credential or tenant store is consulted. Request headers cannot change
its resource or authorization server. Responses use Cache-Control:
no-store and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
scopes_supported contains the three reviewer scopes by default. The
additional erp:read and history:assess scopes appear only when the separate
data-access feature is enabled. Advertising support grants no permission;
each request is independently authenticated and consent checked.
The additional marketplace:read, erp:validate, approval:request and
erp:configure scopes appear only with the connected feature enabled.

404.description: The deployment has not enabled Commerce MCP OAuth

AwsCommerceBearer.description: AWS Commerce API key delivered through approved Marketplace provisioning. Organization and license are server-bound; no caller org_id is accepted.

BearerAuth.description: DECIONIS_API_KEY supplied as an Authorization Bearer credential by the local MCP process, or its private AgentOps access store. The configured or stored organization is bound to that credential.

CommerceOrgCredential.description: The organization's Decionis key (or x-api-key), verified by Core on every request. Accounts-issued Commerce OAuth tokens are accepted on the same resource.

CommerceBearer.description: An organization API key or an enabled, resource-bound Commerce OAuth access token

CommerceApiKey.name: x-api-key
CommerceApiKey.description: Existing organization API key; never supply alongside Authorization

OrganizationId.name: org_id
OrganizationId.description: Organization UUID sourced from the MCP process environment.

ConnectionId.name: connectionId
ConnectionId.description: The Business Central connection Core holds for the caller's key.

mode.description: Scope of this assessment feature, not the broader products or APIs.

cost_scope.description: Merchandise subtotal minus discount and reported item cost; shipping, tax and payment/platform fees excluded.

end.description: Exclusive captured UTC end; exactly 90 days after start.

decision.description: Retrospective rule result only; never permission to execute.

proof_ref.description: Inline historical results are unsigned; no signed proof reference is issued.

transaction_id.description: Opaque, case-sensitive transaction identity. Company prefixes and the complete suffix are preserved during budget reservation lookup.

tenant_id.description: Tenant UUID. The candidate backend normalizes its casing for transaction identity, consistently with the canonical request hash.

timestamp.description: Submitted revision time, included in the canonical request hash. For a configured budget and tracked transaction, a changed request must be strictly newer than the stored revision; exact current retries remain idempotent. This is not an expiry based on the current clock.

reason_code.description: Central policy or budget reason. AGENT_BUDGET_REQUEST_CONFLICT indicates a changed request with an equal or older timestamp for a tracked budget reservation, or multiple stored reservations matching the same identity after tenant UUID casing is normalized. Both leave reservations and spent amount unchanged. It is a BLOCK decision, not a transport failure or evidence of historical overspend.

NativeContext.description: Pinned non-secret expectations from the registered connection. Organization and workspace fields are assertions only; the current workspace key supplies authority. workspace_environment is Core's current classification of its synchronized Accounts workspace, not refreshed provider evidence, and is distinct from environment_name.

NativeConnectionContext.description: Current registered company metadata checked by Core. It does not verify payment facts through Microsoft, refresh provider authority, or grant posting permission.

payment.description: Exactly the commerce-preflight-v2 PAYMENT_RELEASE payload. Each field maps from the ISO 20022 pain.001.001.09 credit transfer the ERP already produces for its bank (paths relative to PmtInf); account elements are never read.

vendor_id.description: pain.001 CdtTrfTxInf/Cdtr/Id/OrgId/Othr/Id, the creditor's id in the ERP

invoice_id.description: pain.001 CdtTrfTxInf/RmtInf/Strd/RfrdDocInf/Nb, only when exactly one referred document is a commercial invoice (CINV)

due_at.description: pain.001 ReqdExctnDt/DtTm, else ReqdExctnDt/Dt at 00:00 UTC

rail.description: pain.001 PmtTpInf/SvcLvl/Cd URGP or SDVA is wire; LclInstrm/Cd CCD, PPD or CTX is ach; SvcLvl/Cd SEPA or NURG is other; otherwise omitted

posted.description: The ledger entry the payment produced, stated by the ERP after posting. Commerce reconciles it against the evaluated payment and records drift when the payment posted while the answer was HOLD or BLOCK, or posted with a different amount, currency or vendor. Never a policy fact; never sent to Decionis.

PaymentEvidence.description: A complete native snapshot with exact journal, payable invoice, beneficiary and funding revisions. Core independently reads the same source and current managed case before authorizing the payment. This envelope is evidence, never caller-provided approval.

source.description: Fresh native environment and company observations, included in the stable snapshot and pre-posting comparison. Optional for earlier records; absence does not prove isolation. Both must be true for the separately authorized self-reviewed sandbox test.

claim_attestation.description: The authority's proof of the claim (compact JWS), when it gave one.

org_id.description: Organization bound to configured or privately stored access. The Commerce Gate MCP sends null so the API derives the tenant from that credential.

amount.description: Monetary action amount. Omitted for non-monetary actions.

channel.description: Who is asking. The Commerce Gate MCP sends mcp; a repricer, ERP job, workflow or direct API integration names itself so the dossier records the actor.

source.description: The tool asking, for the dossier: commercegate-mcp for the MCP, or the name of your repricer, ERP or workflow.

agent_attribution.description: What the calling agent reported about producing the action. Decionis records it on the Decision Dossier as client-reported and unverified; it is never a policy fact and never changes the answer. Sent only when the agent supplies it.

context.description: Bounded normalized action, derived commerce facts, and a nested signals object used by Commerce policies (for example signals.net_margin_percent for a price change). Generic Shadow evaluation does not assert that a connected platform can execute the action.

commerce_action.description: Required with commerce_preflight; must match the top-level action and idempotency key.

commerce_preflight.description: Unreleased opt-in; requires matching client, server and server-owned policy configuration.

org_id.description: Organization bound to configured or privately stored access. The Commerce Gate MCP sends null so the API derives the tenant from that credential.

context.description: The client records the strict submission packet plus derived facts and signals. The packet carries no credentials and does not grant write access to a marketplace.

MarketplaceOfferIdentity.description: Microsoft Partner Center requires an Entra tenant and application identity. AWS Marketplace requires a Login with Amazon subject linked to the seller AWS account and IAM role with offer-management access. The MCP validates that the identity matches the chosen marketplace and never exchanges its credentials.

MarketplacePublicHttpsUrl.description: Public HTTPS URL with no embedded credentials, query parameters, or fragment. The MCP parser enforces those URL restrictions before sending the request.

DecisionDossier.description: Signed decision record returned by the Decionis Protocol API.

DecisionProofPacket.description: Verification material for a Decision Dossier.

ShadowReportDocument.description: Canonical Shadow Mode report document used for row and aggregate views.

HistoricalRateLimit.description: Rate limited; starts allow three requests per minute per licensed organization and grant

checks.name: Order, fulfillment, and return lifecycle eligibility

semantic_constraints: Every result contains exactly one row for each of P01 through P16.
not_applicable and disabled have a null verdict; missing_facts and unsupported require HOLD.
Disposition is BLOCK if any check blocks, otherwise HOLD if any check holds or no check was evaluated, otherwise PROCEED.
Action, facts, idempotency key, policy version and overall verdict must match the request and evidence.
An opt-in request to a backend without this contract fails closed; it must not retry as a legacy evaluation.
